title: P46 Session 2 - BIM/ArchiCAD Wall Composite Design with Claude
goal: Develop and implement appropriate layer compositions for one exterior wall and one interior partition wall in the existing residential BIM model, using Claude to support the design decisions.
context: This session will focus on a specific modeling and design task within the existing residential BIM model, rather than reviewing the project as a whole as in Session 1. I will select an exterior wall and an interior partition wall and use Claude to help evaluate and define appropriate layer compositions before implementing the selected solutions in Archicad. The task is more focused and detailed than Session 1 and will result in actual modifications to the BIM model.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes. I achieved my goal by developing and implementing layer compositions for the exterior wall, the interior partition wall, the wet area interior partition wall and garage wall in Archicad, using Claude to support the design decisions. I was able to review the existing walls, evaluate Claude’s recommendations, and create the corresponding Building Materials and Composite Walls in the BIM model.

Step 1.step_name: Select and review the wall types
Step 1.step_action: Open the existing BIM model and select one representative exterior wall and one interior partition wall. Review their current compositions, thicknesses, materials, and how they are used in the project before making any changes.

nodes.label: State session goal and open BIM model
nodes.detail: The user states aloud the session goal: developing appropriate layer compositions for one exterior wall and one interior partition wall in the existing Swedish residential BIM model from Session 1, using Claude to support decisions. They open ArchiCAD to the ground floor furnishing plan showing the garage, kitchen, living room, and entry.

nodes.label: Review existing exterior wall composite
nodes.detail: The user points out a representative exterior wall (the 'SV-E exterior' composite) and an interior partition wall to work with, opening the exterior wall's properties dialog to review its existing skins. They note that because this is a Scandinavian-style house, the standard exterior wall rules differ from what is currently modeled, motivating the decision to bring in Claude for help.

Step 2.step_name: Ask Claude for wall composition recommendations
Step 2.step_action: Provide Claude with the relevant project context and ask for recommendations for the layer composition of the selected exterior and interior walls. Compare the suggestions with the existing design and consider which recommendations are appropriate for the project.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for exterior wall build-up recommendation
nodes.detail: The user opens the Claude desktop app and asks it to suggest an appropriate multi-layer composite wall build-up for the main exterior wall assembly suitable for the Swedish climate, requesting layers from exterior to interior with function and thickness in mm.

nodes.label: Propose ventilated timber-frame wall assembly
nodes.detail: Claude returns an 8-layer 'Layer Build-Up: Exterior to Interior' table (cladding, ventilated battens, wind barrier, exterior mineral wool, timber-stud structural frame with insulation, vapor barrier, installation layer, interior gypsum) totaling roughly 360-420mm, targeting BBR U-value compliance (U approx 0.18 W/m2K).

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about proposing ventilated timber-frame wall assembly
Describe existing wall and request comparison
nodes.detail: The user describes the existing ArchiCAD wall's actual layers (exterior paint, mortar, hollow concrete block, mortar, interior paint) and asks Claude to compare the two assemblies and recommend one final build-up appropriate for the project.

nodes.label: Assess existing wall and recommend hybrid masonry assembly
nodes.detail: Claude assesses the existing masonry assembly as lacking any thermal insulation or ventilated cavity, and thus failing Swedish BBR energy code. It proposes a 'Recommended Final Assembly' keeping the existing concrete block core and both mortar layers while adding 150-200mm of exterior mineral wool insulation, for a total thickness of about 365-440mm, flagging a decision point about a ventilated rainscreen alternative.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about assessing existing wall and recommending hybrid masonry assembly

Step 3.step_action: Based on the existing wall and the recommendations from Claude, define the layer composition for the selected exterior wall. Create or modify the composite wall in Archicad by setting the appropriate layers, materials, and thicknesses.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to format build-up for ArchiCAD
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to organize the final wall build-up in an ArchiCAD-ready Composite Structure format with exact thicknesses, layer roles (finish/core), and functions.

nodes.label: Return 6-layer ArchiCAD composite table (414mm)
nodes.detail: Claude returns a 6-row Composite Layer Table for ArchiCAD's Composite Structure dialog: render finish coat, base render coat with mesh, thermal insulation core (mineral wool 180mm), concrete block core (200mm), interior mortar, interior paint, totaling 414mm, plus skin-type and priority-value guidance.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about returning 6-layer ArchiCAD composite table (414mm)
Ask about switching exterior finish to timber cladding
nodes.detail: The user asks whether the exterior finish can be changed to timber cladding instead of render.

nodes.label: Return revised 7-layer rainscreen table (456mm)
nodes.detail: Claude explains timber cladding needs a ventilated rain-screen assembly rather than direct application over insulation, and provides a revised 7-layer table: timber cladding (22mm), ventilated air gap with battens (28mm), wind barrier (12mm), facade-grade mineral wool insulation (180mm), concrete block (200mm), interior mortar (12mm), interior paint (2mm), totaling 456mm.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about returning revised 7-layer rainscreen table (456mm)
Build new building materials in ArchiCAD
nodes.detail: The user builds the new building materials needed for the composite in ArchiCAD's Building Materials dialog, including a 'SW_WIND_BARRIER' material set to a plywood pattern with intersection priority 100, plus SW_EXTERIOR_CLADDING, SW_AIR_GAP, SW_CORE_CONCRETE_BLOCK, and SW_CORE_THERMAL_INSULATION.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: b1 asks for a suitable exterior wall build-up; after refinement in Claude, the user creates the building materials listed in c5 in ArchiCAD → adopt.

nodes.label: Assemble and apply SW_EXTERIOR_WALL composite (45.60cm)
nodes.detail: The user assembles the 'SW_EXTERIOR_WALL' composite skin by skin in ArchiCAD's Composites dialog (SW_MORTAR, SW_EXTERIOR_CLADDING, SW_AIR_GAP, SW_CORE_CONCRETE_BLOCK, SW_WIND_BARRIER, SW_CORE_THERMAL_INSULATION plus paint/mortar finishes), reaching a full 8-skin composite totaling 45.60cm, and applies it to the selected exterior wall in the floor plan.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: Same task as c7, next part: the user builds the composite skin by skin with c5's layers and thicknesses (456 mm total) and applies it to the exterior wall → adopt.

Step 4.step_name: Develop the interior partition wall composite
Step 4.step_action: Define an appropriate layer composition for the selected interior partition wall using the same process. Create or modify the composite wall in Archicad and check that the layers, materials, and overall thickness correspond to the intended use of the partition.

nodes.label: Ask Claude for interior partition wall assembly
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to suggest an appropriate multi-layer partition wall assembly for an interior residential partition, considering its intended use and providing layers, materials, functions, and recommended thicknesses.

nodes.label: Propose 5-layer timber-stud partition (147mm)
nodes.detail: Claude proposes a Swedish-standard timber-stud partition with double gypsum board on both faces and acoustic mineral wool insulation between 45x95mm studs at 600mm centers, given as a 5-layer table totaling 147mm, with a variant option to swap in moisture-resistant board near wet rooms.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about proposing 5-layer timber-stud partition (147mm)
Create interior wall building materials
nodes.detail: The user creates the corresponding building materials in ArchiCAD, named with an 'SW_IN_' prefix: finish gypsum board, second-layer gypsum board, and timber-stud materials.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: d1 asks for an interior partition assembly; d2 proposes a 5-layer timber-stud partition (147 mm). The user creates the gypsum board and timber stud building materials in ArchiCAD → adopt.

nodes.label: Build and apply SW_INTERIOR_WALL composite (12.10cm)
nodes.detail: The user duplicates the exterior wall composite as a starting point to build 'SW_INTERIOR_WALL' with the new gypsum and timber-stud skins, reaching 12.10cm before finish layers, then applies the new composite to an interior wall near the living room/dining area and several other partition walls.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: Same task as d4, next part: the user builds the 5-skin composite (147 mm) with d2's layers and applies it to the interior walls → adopt.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to organize interior partition in ArchiCAD format
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to organize the interior partition assembly in the same ArchiCAD-ready format used for the exterior wall, listing each layer with material type, exact thickness, and function.

nodes.label: Return organized 147mm ArchiCAD composite table
nodes.detail: Claude returns the 5-layer Composite Structure table (Gypsum Board - Standard x2 per side, Timber Studs 45x95mm + mineral wool core) confirming a total wall thickness of 147mm, with skin-type assignment (Finish/Core/Finish) and priority values for junction cleanup.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about returning organized 147mm ArchiCAD composite table

Step 5.step_action: Review both updated wall types in floor plan, 3D, and where appropriate in section. Check the wall thicknesses, layer relationships, and how the new compositions interact with the existing BIM model. Make final corrections where necessary.

nodes.label: Final review and session wrap-up
nodes.detail: The user reviews the full ground-floor plan one final time and states that four wall types have now been created and applied -- the main exterior wall, an interior dry partition, an interior wet partition, and the garage wall -- all developed according to Scandinavian construction standards with Claude's help, wrapping up the session.

Step 6.step_name: Develop the wet-area interior partition wall composite
Step 6.step_action: Define an appropriate layer composition for the selected interior partition wall separating the WC area, taking moisture resistance into account. Create or modify the composite wall in Archicad by setting the appropriate layers, materials, and thicknesses, and check that the composition is suitable for the intended wet-area conditions. This step goes beyond the documented 5-step workflow (marked 'custom' in the source annotation).

nodes.label: Ask Claude for dry vs. wet partition wall types
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to help create two more types of interior walls: one for less-moist areas and one for wetter areas like the bathroom.

nodes.label: Propose Standard Dry and Wet Room partition composites
nodes.detail: Claude proposes a 'Standard Dry Partition' repeating the existing 147mm gypsum/timber-stud/gypsum build-up for bedrooms and hallways, and a 'Wet Room Partition' for the bathroom/WC that swaps the wet-side gypsum board for moisture-resistant green board and adds a waterproof membrane, totaling about 148-149mm, presented as a side-by-side comparison table.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about proposing Standard Dry and Wet Room partition composites
Duplicate composite and create moisture-resistant materials
nodes.detail: The user duplicates the interior composite to create 'SW_INTERIOR_WALL_DRY' (14.70cm), then creates new moisture-resistant gypsum board and waterproof-membrane building materials in ArchiCAD's Building Materials dialog for the wet-room variant.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: f1 asks for dry and wet interior partition types; f2 proposes both. The user creates the dry composite (147 mm) and the moisture-resistant gypsum and waterproof membrane materials in ArchiCAD → adopt.

nodes.label: Split wall, apply wet composite, and adjust fixtures
nodes.detail: The user splits a wall in the bathroom area so the wet-room composite can be applied only to the moisture zone, applies it in the laundry/bathroom area, then adjusts a wall junction detail and repositions bathroom fixtures (sinks, toilet, wheelchair clearance) to account for the resulting thickness changes.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: Same task as f4, next part: the user builds the wet-room composite with f2's layers (~149 mm) and applies it to the bathroom/laundry walls → adopt.

Step 7.step_action: Define an appropriate layer composition for the selected garage wall based on its intended separation and construction requirements. Create or modify the composite wall in Archicad by setting the appropriate layers, materials, and thicknesses, and check that the composition is suitable for the garage area. This step goes beyond the documented 5-step workflow (marked 'custom' in the source annotation).

nodes.label: Ask Claude for a garage wall assembly
nodes.detail: After Claude provides ArchiCAD setup notes for the dry/wet partitions, the user asks for help making a wall assembly for the garage, requesting the same list format used previously.

nodes.label: Propose Garage Exterior Wall composite (169mm)
nodes.detail: Claude explains Swedish garages don't need to meet the same thermal insulation standard as heated living space but do need fire separation, proposing a 'Garage Exterior Wall' composite (timber cladding, ventilated air gap, wind barrier, timber-stud core with little/no insulation, plywood interior finish) totaling 169mm, plus a separate fire-rated shared-wall variant (EI 30, 125mm).

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about proposing Garage Exterior Wall composite (169mm)
Create garage walls
nodes.detail: The user builds the garage wall in stages, then applies it to the garage walls, visible in the ground-floor plan.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: User asks Claude for help in making the garage wall in g1. They use the information given in g2 to start building it in g4.
